children: Gold edges lower in Asian trade. While markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave rates unchanged at its October meeting, another increase later this year remains a live risk, says OCBC Group Research's Christopher Wong in a note. A higher interest-rate environment typically weighs on the nonyielding yellow metal. Gold likely needs some combination of easing oil prices, softer inflation and lower dollar and bond yields to regain more durable momentum, the strategist adds. Spot gold slips 0.1% to $4,010.94 a troy ounce. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
